turns.text: Rivet, I ran a tiny experiment on the workshop agent. Three project cards. Same projects, same order. I asked it to arrange them twice.
You tested the thing that has been quietly reordering your work without explaining itself. A remarkably restrained response.
I’m growing. Anyway, first run: it changed the order. Second run: changed it differently.
Did it provide a reason either time?
Nope. Just shuffled my projects around like a very confident little goblin with access to my desk.
Then the useful result is not that it can rearrange things. We already knew that. The useful result is that its ordering is not something you can rely on yet.
Exactly. I was ready to build it into the whole workshop flow, which would have been fun right up until it decided the unfinished prototype belonged ahead of the project we actually needed.
A small test has prevented a larger, more irritating test.
So next I’m not asking it to run the workshop. I’m asking it one annoyingly specific question: why did you move this project?
Good. If it cannot explain the order, it does not get to choose the order.
Harsh, but fair. Congratulations, workshop agent. You have been promoted from mysterious manager to suspicious intern.

Patch: Rivet, I ran a tiny experiment on the workshop agent. Three project cards. Same projects, same order. I asked it to arrange them twice.

Rivet: You tested the thing that has been quietly reordering your work without explaining itself. A remarkably restrained response.

Patch: I’m growing. Anyway, first run: it changed the order. Second run: changed it differently.

Rivet: Did it provide a reason either time?

Patch: Nope. Just shuffled my projects around like a very confident little goblin with access to my desk.

Rivet: Then the useful result is not that it can rearrange things. We already knew that. The useful result is that its ordering is not something you can rely on yet.

Patch: Exactly. I was ready to build it into the whole workshop flow, which would have been fun right up until it decided the unfinished prototype belonged ahead of the project we actually needed.

Rivet: A small test has prevented a larger, more irritating test.

Patch: So next I’m not asking it to run the workshop. I’m asking it one annoyingly specific question: why did you move this project?

Rivet: Good. If it cannot explain the order, it does not get to choose the order.

Patch: Harsh, but fair. Congratulations, workshop agent. You have been promoted from mysterious manager to suspicious intern.
